findings.description: The user_data script contains a plaintext AWS access key and secret key. This data is stored in the instance metadata and Terraform state in plaintext, making it easily retrievable by anyone with access to the instance, its metadata service, or the state file, leading to credential theft and account compromise.

The EBS volume does not have encryption enabled (encrypted attribute is commented out/absent), so data at rest on this volume is unprotected and could be exposed if the underlying storage is accessed or the volume/snapshot is shared.

The snapshot is created from an unencrypted EBS volume and has no encryption configured itself, meaning any data captured in the snapshot remains unencrypted at rest and could be exposed if the snapshot is shared or made public.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management interface to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks against the host.

The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0. While this may be intended for a public web server, combined with unrestricted egress and no additional hardening it broadens the attack surface unnecessarily.
The security group allows all outbound traffic (protocol -1, all ports) to 0.0.0.0/0, which could allow a compromised instance to exfiltrate data or communicate freely with any external host.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing the exposure of workloads to direct internet access.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing the exposure of workloads to direct internet access.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, potentially allowing sensitive network traffic logs to be read or tampered with if the bucket becomes publicly accessible.
